transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is... well, it’s probably just normal stress, I mean, everyone gets a little scattered sometimes, right? 

But I manage a clinic, and lately, I'll start working on an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in a metrics meeting with every intention of tracking the information. But within just a few minutes, my mind just... drifts. It drifts so far that I end up rereading the exact same numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the whole point of the discussion. 

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really do try to stay on top of things and be a good employee. I hope I'm explaining that right—does that make sense?
Did you have the same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Oh, um... well, I suppose a little bit? I mean, I was a good kid, I always tried really hard to be good and do what I was told. But... yeah, even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers writing notes on my report cards saying that I was bright—which was very nice of them to say—but that I was... careless. 

I hate using that word, honestly, because it makes it sound like I didn't care, and I really did! But my mother actually used to have to sit right next to me while I finished my homework. I would just... I'd lose track of what the actual assignments were, or I'd get home and realize I completely forgot to bring my books back from school. 

She was so patient with me, and I feel a little bad even bringing it up, to be honest. I mean, a lot of kids are a little forgetful like that, right? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Oh, um, worrying? No, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I care about things, obviously, and I want everything at the clinic to run smoothly, but I don't sit around agonizing over things that haven't happened. 

I try to stay pretty positive, actually. I think it's important to keep a good attitude, especially when you're managing a team. I mean, everyone has normal, everyday concerns, but it doesn't keep me up at night or anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? I just try to take things as they come.
Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?

Oh, depressed? No, no, definitely not. I mean, I have days where I feel a little frustrated with myself for getting so behind on my reports, but that's just me needing to try harder, you know? 

I really try to be a cheerful person, especially at work. I wouldn't want my staff to think I'm unhappy or anything. So, no, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed at all. I hope that's helpful? I'm just trying to give you the right information.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of inattentive symptoms causing occupational impairment, with clear retrospective evidence of similar symptoms in childhood. Symptoms include drifting attention during meetings and reports, rereading material repeatedly, missing key discussion points, losing track of assignments, forgetting books, and being described as careless despite effort. Anxiety and depressive disorders were specifically screened and denied, making ADHD predominantly inattentive presentation the best fit.
